Definition: a vehicle; by implication, a team; by extension, cavalry; by analogy a rider, i.e. the upper millstone
BiblicalUsage: The Egyptians pursued with all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots and his horsemen, and the sea covered them. Elijah went up by a whirlwind, and there appeared a chariot of fire and horses of fire that parted him from Elisha. Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will remember the name of the LORD our God, and woe to them that go down to Egypt for help and stay on horses and trust in chariots.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the chariot is the Bible's picture of power you can see, and that is exactly why it fails. Pharaoh's chariots sank, Elijah's chariot rose, and the difference was whose hand held the reins. I will not trust in chariots, because the God who drowned an army and carried a prophet is the only strength that does not break.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
